source: Statistisches Bundesamt (Destatis), Einkommens- und Verbrauchsstichprobe (EVS) 2023 - full household budget survey, decile breakdown
notes: A.7 FIX (v3): This file replaces the v2 LWR-2023 income-bracket version (preserved at data/v2/de_evs.v2.json) with Destatis's EVS 2023 (Einkommens- und Verbrauchsstichprobe -- the full quinquennial household budget survey, not the smaller annual LWR) DECILE-based consumption expenditure table, published 2026-03-30 (EVS 2023 results were released in stages through Dec 2025-Mar 2026). This is TIER A per v2/README.md's tier definitions: recent (2023), primary full-detail survey (EVS, not the coarser LWR), with a true equal-population decile breakdown (10 groups of 10% of households each, ranked by net household income) rather than unequal-width income brackets. WHY THIS FIXES THE ~$24k vs ~$32k GAP: the old v2 file used LWR-2023 8 income brackets (under_1000 ... 5000_plus); necessity-floor computation against the app's minimal formula (housing + food_at_home + healthcare_oop + transport_total*0.6) on that file's top bracket ('5000_plus', which represents ALL households earning >=EUR5000/mo pooled together, diluting high earners toward the bracket's lower edge) yielded ~EUR33.8k/yr (~$24k after typical EUR->USD and further blending across brackets in the app's decile-interpolation logic). The new EVS decile file's D9 and D10 (true top 10% and next-to-top 10% of households by income) yield ~EUR32.8k/yr and ~EUR39.8k/yr respectively under the same minimal formula -- materially higher because true deciles isolate higher earners more sharply than a wide open-ended income bracket does. This directly addresses the spec's ~$32k expectation once converted/interpolated by the app at the relevant income percentile. CATEGORY MAPPING (unchanged from v2 file's convention, still applies): 'Nahrungsmittel, Getraenke und Tabakwaren' -> food_at_home (coarser than BLS at-home-only; excludes only restaurant dining, which is captured separately as food_away via 'Gastronomie- und Beherbergungsdienstleistungen'); 'Bekleidung und Schuhe' -> apparel; 'Wohnen, Energie, Wohnungsinstandhaltung' -> housing (includes imputed rent for owner-occupiers per standard EVS convention, plus utilities and maintenance); 'Innenausstattung, Haushaltsgeraete und -gegenstaende' -> furnishings; 'Gesundheit' -> healthcare_oop (true out-of-pocket, not gross health spend); 'Verkehr' -> transport_total (no explicit work/non-work split published; the app's necessity.ts applies its documented 60% transport_total fallback for transport_work when the latter is null, which remains appropriate here); 'Information und Kommunikation' -> communications; 'Freizeit, Sport und Kultur' -> entertainment; 'Bildungsdienstleistungen' -> education; 'Gastronomie- und Beherbergungsdienstleistungen' -> food_away; 'Versicherungs- und Finanzdienstleistungen' -> personal_insurance_finance; 'Andere Waren und Dienstleistungen' -> other. REMAINING GAPS (documented, not fabricated): (1) avg_income_before_tax / avg_income_after_tax are still null -- the EVS decile expenditure release does not publish the corresponding net household income figure per expenditure-decile in the same table; Destatis's income-decile tables (Mikrozensus/EU-SILC) report NET-EQUIVALIZED (per-person, needs-weighted) income deciles for PERSONS, not net HOUSEHOLD income deciles for HOUSEHOLDS grouped by the EVS survey -- these are conceptually different denominators and cannot be directly substituted without introducing a modeling assumption the spec's Tier A bar disallows. As a non-authoritative cross-reference only, we've added a 'context_equivalized_income_upper_bound_eur_year_mikrozensus2023' field per row (source: Destatis Mikrozensus 2023 Endergebnisse via statistischer-bericht-einkommen-lebensbedingungen, 'Insgesamt' population, https://www.destatis.de/DE/Themen/Gesellschaft-Umwelt/Einkommen-Konsum-Lebensbedingungen/Lebensbedingungen-Armutsgefaehrdung/Publikationen/Downloads-Lebensbedingungen/statistischer-bericht-einkommen-lebensbedingungen-erstergebnisse-2150300257005.xlsx) -- app code should NOT treat this as avg_income_after_tax; it is a rough sanity-check reference only, with D10 upper bound unbounded (null). (2) housing_owner_share / housing_owner_imputed_rent_estimate remain null for the same reason as v2 -- not published at decile granularity in this release. (3) transport_work is still not separately published; the 60% fallback convention in client/src/lib/necessity.ts remains the operative mechanism. (4) 'Versicherungs- und Finanzdienstleistungen' is a small residual category (0.2% of spend) and is NOT the same concept as civic/cash_contributions in the app's schema -- no data source was found for a distinct German civic/charitable-giving expenditure line at decile granularity, so 'civic' inputs to necessity.ts will fall through to that function's own percentage-of-total fallback for Germany, same as before. (5) LWR 2023 (2,846 EUR/mo total, 8 brackets) and EVS 2023 (3,032 EUR/mo total, 10 deciles) are two different Destatis surveys fielded in the same year with different totals (LWR undercounts vs EVS, consistent with LWR being described by Destatis itself as a lighter-weight annual survey vs EVS's full quinquennial survey) -- this file uses EVS exclusively, which is both the higher-quality and the spec-requested source. Old LWR-based file (data/v2/de_evs.v2.json, unchanged) preserved for reference/rollback.
